From: Jim Hardy <jim.hardy@brightline.com>

Cc: audits@brightline.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SCIM sync deviation observed during SOC 2 readiness check

Diego,

During our automated validation for SOC 2 readiness we picked up a recurring SCIM sync deviation between Redwood's provisioning service and Brightline's identity store. The deviations look like: missing role assignments for ~1.2% of accounts and intermittent attribute overwrites (jobTitle and dept) for a small subset of users.

I attached a diff extract (scim_delta_diff.csv) that shows 24 user records over the last 72 hours where the delta applied out of order — leading to transient privilege expansion in one case. This is a blocker for our SOC 2 testing team until we can demonstrate root cause analysis and a remediation plan.

Can you confirm ownership of the provisioning pipeline and provide: 1) a short timeline of what happened, 2) the relevant service account and runbook, and 3) logs for the delta apply window (2026-11-02 03:00:00 to 2026-11-05 02:59:59 UTC)?

We can schedule a quick call if that's faster. Appreciate your help — SOC 2 audit is on a tight timeline for Brightline.

Thanks,
Jim
Security Auditor, Brightline

Attachments: scim_delta_diff.csv (CSV excerpt, 24 rows)

Jim / team — quick technical findings from the first pass. I pulled node logs and the delta-apply trace for the period 2026-11-02 02:50:00 -> 2026-11-05 03:10:00 UTC and attached scim_delta_diff.csv (trimmed). Observations: 

- Root cause hypothesis: a race condition in the delta ingestion queue when multiple provisioning events for the same externalId arrive within a 3s window; our worker reorders events if retries occur and we don't persist a strict sequence token per externalId.
- Impact: attribute overwrite (jobTitle/department) in 18 accounts; a temporary role elevation in 1 account that was reverted within 7 minutes by a subsequent delta.
- Mitigations in flight: 1) short-term: enable sequenceToken persistence for deltas keyed by externalId (toggle deployed to canaries); 2) mid-term: backfill fix that rejects out-of-order deltas by checking lastSequence on apply.

I'll include the exact node IDs and truncated logs in the shared drive link (see below). For SOC 2 evidence, I propose we deliver: 1) the full delta logs, 2) the new canary deployment verification, and 3) a remediation timeline plus change request entry for INF-4621.

Deliverables ETA: full logs + mapping spreadsheet by Mon 2026-11-08 EOD; remediation PR + canary verification by Tue 2026-11-09 EOD.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
